coalition_partners.desc: They ask for extra money for settlement in the territories.

coalition_partners.label: A national unity government with the main rival party
coalition_partners.desc: A broad government: the rival party asks for a senior security portfolio.

promotion_note: fix-cabinet (v2 fixes): promotions are national programmes with an era (from/until) and the programme tags of the governing bloc (labour, right, centre) that favours them; a new government of the same party (or a rotation) keeps its ministers' programmes.
terms_note: fix-cabinet: 'how' is election, succession (new PM, no election), rotation, unity (opposition joins without an election) or reformed (coalition rebuilt after a break-up); 'party' is the prime minister's party. Dates: Knesset, Governments of Israel (S1133).

religious_zionist.desc: It asks for the religious services, its schools and a say over Sabbath and marriage law.

haredi.desc: It asks for yeshiva budgets, independent schools and draft exemptions.

centre.desc: It asks for market reforms and lower taxes for the middle class.

left.desc: It asks for welfare, civil rights and a push for negotiations.

labour_ally.desc: A labour-movement party: it asks for development, the kibbutzim and workers' housing.

right_settlement.desc: It asks for settlement in the territories and a harder line abroad.

immigrant.desc: An immigrants' party: it asks for absorption budgets, housing and recognition of degrees.

arab.desc: It asks for development plans for Arab towns, housing and policing.

rival_major.desc: The main rival party joins a broad government and asks for senior portfolios.
